questions.query: Does a Hilbert or Morton generation field make one continuous infinite corridor, and do its tiles change at negative chunk boundaries?
facts: Hilbert guarantees edge adjacency between consecutive ranks inside a finite power-of-two tile only; repeated tiles do not promise a continuous infinite Hilbert curve. Morton interleaves coordinates and successive ranks need not share an edge.
Orders 1 through 20 and integer cell sizes 1 through 4096 use signed floor tiling at absolute coordinates, independently of the output chunk partition.
The separately defined macrocell hub/port network owns interconnected procedural routes. Curve fields can guide masks, parameters or material variation without replacing that network.

Application times one-minus-exclusion times strength, context predicate and shape is captured once per modifier and reused for guidance and material output. Earlier modifiers cannot feed back into later context masks.

Missing references and cycles, including warp references, reject; warp shifts only the receiving primitive rather than recursively resampling dependencies. Global exclusions stay authoritative, hard geometry is reapplied after guidance, and hard material is final.

questions.query: Do procedural aggregate definitions create new mixture physics, and does grain_size quantize a named variation field?

Without a variation field, a seed-and-ID hash selects one material per signed world-aligned grain. A named variation field selects directly at each sample; grain_size does not quantize it.

Canonical recipes retain authored weights separately from prepared normalized selection. Zero, invalid IDs, duplicate components and normalization underflow reject; weights express preferences rather than finite-crop quotas.

questions.query: Does hiding a generator modifier or selecting a diagnostic bypass budgets, and can an old inspection packet enter a new preview or live World?
